title: Hearing Ellington as the Washingtonians
summary: Tate remembers a clipping about Paul Whiteman tipping Duke's band and why he preferred Fletcher's sound at first.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: One band that we haven't mentioned at all, it was Ellington. Now were you conscious of Duke?
Of Duke? Yes, yes, when he called himself the Washingtonians.

I read a write-up one time. I didn't know who they were, but I read some comments and -- I got to pull these off -- I read some comments that Paul Whiteman had given to him and I think he gave him a hundred dollars or something and that was in one of the papers. I'll never forget, I can't remember nothing except the Washingtonians, Paul Whiteman said, "Gee, that sound these cats get," and he went somewhere and he gave them a hundred-dollar tip. I don't think at that time he had six or seven pieces, maybe eight pieces or something like that. They didn't call it Duke Ellington, they just said the Washingtonian. And then I -- you know, I would listen to his records and -- but it was different from Fletcher.
